The show's enduring dominance—scoring 90 out of 100 across 43 reviews—demonstrates its staying power as a cultural phenomenon that transcends typical Broadway fare.

Among newer productions, **Maybe Happy Ending** stands out as a critical darling, with reviewers praising this robot love story as one of the most original musicals to debut in years. Meanwhile, **Oh, Mary!**, Cole Escola's absurdist reimagining of Mary Todd Lincoln as a boozy cabaret enthusiast, proves that irreverent comedy has found a enthusiastic audience this season.

The month also showcases Broadway's ability to sustain long-running productions without sacrificing quality. **The Lion King** and **The Book of Mormon** both maintain strong critical scores, while **Chicago**'s stripped-down revival continues to feel surprisingly vital. The timely **Ragtime** revival brings renewed relevance to its historical narrative, with particular praise directed toward Joshua Henry's powerhouse performance.

From the folk-opera innovation of **Hadestown** to the spectacular stagecraft of **Harry Potter and the Cursed Child**, March 2026 offers theatergoers an unusually diverse range of highly-rated options. Whether you're drawn to hip-hop history lessons, robot romance, or mythological retellings, this month's Broadway landscape rewards both first-time visitors and seasoned theater enthusiasts.

best-broadway-plays.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays: March 2026

As Broadway moves through the spring season of 2026, the dramatic landscape offers an eclectic mix of original comedies, magical spectacles, and franchise expansions. This month's selection of four plays averages a solid 75 out of 100 from critics, reflecting a range of theatrical ambitions and execution.

Leading the pack is **Oh, Mary!**, Cole Escola's absurdist comedy that reimagines Mary Todd Lincoln as a cabaret-obsessed, hard-drinking narcissist. With an 84/100 rating across 33 reviews, the farce earns consistent praise for its riotous humor and irreverent take on historical drama. Critics highlight Escola's sharp comedic voice and the production's willingness to push boundaries.

Close behind is **Harry Potter and the Cursed Child**, which maintains its position as a technical marvel. Scoring 82/100 across 69 reviews, the two-part play continues to impress audiences with its spectacular stagecraft and magical illusions, though critics note the story itself remains uneven. The production's visual achievements compensate for narrative shortcomings, making it a crowd-pleaser for fans of theatrical spectacle.

**Stranger Things: The First Shadow** brings Netflix's hit series to the stage with ambitious technical wizardry and special effects that critics acknowledge as impressive. However, at 66/100 across 35 reviews, the three-hour prequel struggles with pacing and narrative coherence, suggesting that not all screen-to-stage adaptations translate seamlessly.

Whether you're drawn to audacious comedy, magical stagecraft, or franchise storytelling, this month's offerings provide multiple entry points into Broadway's current dramatic conversation. Consider your tolerance for runtime and narrative complexity when choosing your next theatrical experience.

best-new-broadway-shows.intro:

As Broadway moves deeper into the spring season, March 2026 brings an eclectic mix of revivals and intimate new works to the stage. Leading the pack is a revival of **Ragtime**, which earns strong critical praise for its timely resonance and commanding performances. Joshua Henry's powerhouse turn anchors a production that critics find both musically stirring and dramatically urgent, proving that Terrence McNally and Lynn Ahrens' epic remains as relevant as ever.

On the opposite end of the theatrical spectrum, **Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across New York)** demonstrates that Broadway audiences still have an appetite for modest, character-driven storytelling. This British import—a sincere two-hander rom-com—wins critics over with its heartfelt simplicity and authentic performances, offering a welcome counterpoint to larger productions.

The revival of **Chess** divides critical opinion, though few dispute the vocal firepower of its star-studded cast. While Lea Michele, Aaron Tveit, and the ensemble deliver the ABBA-penned score with technical brilliance, reviewers remain split on whether the production successfully clarifies the musical's notoriously convoluted book.

With an average critic score of 73/100 across featured productions, March presents a solid if unspectacular lineup that favors proven material and star performances over experimental risks. Whether you're drawn to sweeping historical narratives, intimate romantic comedies, or Cold War-era rock operas, this month's Broadway landscape offers multiple entry points for theatergoers seeking their next show.

best-broadway-shows-2020.intro:

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway shows that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of theater interrupted—productions that launched just before or amid unprecedented global disruption, yet managed to leave their mark on the cultural landscape.

Among the five notable productions from that year, **Les Misérables** stands out with the highest critical reception, earning an 83/100 from reviewers. This grittier reboot at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre demonstrates how classic material can be successfully reimagined for contemporary audiences, though the approach doesn't win over every critic.

**A Soldier's Play** represents a significant milestone, bringing Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama to Broadway for the first time in a revival that critics widely celebrate for its continued relevance and powerful performances. With 29 reviews averaging 78/100, the production proves that some stories only grow more urgent with time.

The year's offerings reveal Broadway's range, from Laura Linney's solo turn in **My Name is Lucy Barton** (which divides critics despite universal praise for its star) to the more conventional pleasures of **Grand Horizons**' ensemble comedy. Meanwhile, Ivo van Hove's polarizing **West Side Story** reimagining demonstrates the risks and rewards of radical reinterpretation.

With an average critic score of 74/100 across these five productions, the class of 2020 represents solid, if not spectacular, theatrical achievement—work that managed to premiere during one of the most challenging periods in Broadway history. For theatergoers interested in understanding how Broadway navigated this pivotal moment, these productions offer essential viewing and context.

best-broadway-shows-2021.intro:

The year's most critically acclaimed productions span an impressive range, from intimate experimental works to grand theatrical spectacles. Leading the pack is "Dana H.," Lucas Hnath's unconventional docudrama featuring Deirdre O'Connell's mesmerizing lip-sync performance to a real-life interview, which critics describe as both haunting and unforgettable. Meanwhile, "The Phantom of the Opera" proves that Andrew Lloyd Webber's mega-musical remains a spectacular crowd-pleaser despite—or perhaps because of—its unapologetic camp. Rebecca Frecknall's immersive reimagining of "Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club" transforms the Playhouse Theatre itself into the show's centerpiece, earning widespread acclaim for its bold vision.

The 2021 season also showcased powerful solo performances in "Lackawanna Blues," Sam Mendes's epic staging of "The Lehman Trilogy," and Tina Satter's verbatim thriller "Is This A Room." Marianne Elliott's gender-swapped "Company" brought fresh vitality to Sondheim's classic, while "Pass Over" earned its place as Broadway's symbolic reopening production. The pop-concert energy of "SIX" and Lynn Nottage's compassionate "Clyde's" round out a diverse slate.

With an average critic score of 81/100 across these ten productions, the class of 2021 demonstrates both artistic ambition and broad appeal. Whether you're drawn to experimental docudrama, reimagined classics, or bold new voices, these productions offer compelling reasons to experience Broadway's post-pandemic renaissance.

best-broadway-plays-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of theater interrupted—productions that launched just before or amid unprecedented challenges, yet managed to leave lasting impressions on critics and audiences alike.

Leading our rankings is **Les Misérables** (83/100), a grittier reboot at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre that reimagines the beloved musical with a darker, more visceral approach. While not all critics embrace the radical departure from the original production, the majority praise its bold vision and technical achievements.

**A Soldier's Play** (78/100) stands as perhaps the most significant theatrical event of the year, bringing Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama to Broadway for the first time in a sterling revival. Critics widely acclaim this production for demonstrating the enduring relevance of Fuller's examination of race, power, and identity within the military—themes that resonate as powerfully today as when the play was written.

The remaining productions showcase Broadway's range: Laura Linney commands the stage in the polarizing solo adaptation **My Name is Lucy Barton** (71/100), while **Grand Horizons** (71/100) offers more traditional boulevard comedy elevated by veteran performers Jane Alexander and James Cromwell. Rounding out the list, Ivo van Hove's controversial **West Side Story** (68/100) reimagining proves that even canonical works can spark fierce debate about interpretation and innovation.

With an average critic score of 74/100 across these five productions, the plays of 2020 demonstrate both artistic ambition and the enduring power of live theater to provoke, comfort, and challenge audiences in equal measure.

best-broadway-plays-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2021

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway season of 2021 stands as a watershed moment in theater history—not merely because it marked the industry's reopening after an unprecedented shutdown, but because it delivered an extraordinarily diverse slate of productions that challenged conventions and redefined what Broadway could be.

The ten standout shows from that year, averaging an impressive 81/100 critical score, range from experimental docudramas to beloved revivals, each contributing something vital to the theatrical landscape. Leading the pack is **Dana H.**, Lucas Hnath's unconventional docudrama featuring Deirdre O'Connell's mesmerizing lip-sync performance that critics consistently describe as unforgettable. Close behind, **The Phantom of the Opera** proved that spectacle and melody still have their place, while **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club** demonstrated how immersive reimagining can breathe new life into classic material.

What's particularly striking about 2021's offerings is their breadth: virtuosic solo performances like **Lackawanna Blues**, epic dramas such as **The Lehman Trilogy**, verbatim theater in **Is This a Room**, and bold revivals including the gender-swapped **Company**. The season also featured Antoinette Chinonye Nwandu's **Pass Over** as Broadway's symbolic reopening show, the pop-infused **SIX**, and Lynn Nottage's heartfelt **Clyde's**.

Whether you're drawn to experimental theater that pushes boundaries, spectacular musicals that embrace tradition, or intimate dramas that examine the human condition, 2021's Broadway season offers essential theatrical experiences that continue to resonate nearly five years later.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2022

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway season of 2022 stands out as a remarkable year that brought fresh voices and celebrated revivals to the stage in equal measure. This collection of ten productions, averaging an impressive 83/100 critical score, showcases a season defined by Pulitzer Prize winners, inventive revivals, and fearlessly original new works.

Leading the pack is **Kimberly Akimbo**, the quirky musical that critics consistently describe as a near-perfect balance of comedy and heartbreak. Close behind, **Into the Woods** proves that stripped-down revivals can honor Sondheim's legacy while feeling utterly contemporary, while **A Strange Loop** pushes boundaries with Michael R. Jackson's brazenly honest, meta-theatrical storytelling.

Beyond A Strange Loop's recent win, the year featured revivals and productions of **Topdog/Underdog**, **Leopoldstadt**, **Between Riverside and Crazy**, **How I Learned to Drive**, and **Cost of Living**—each bringing essential American drama to Broadway stages with renewed urgency and insight. Suzan-Lori Parks' Pulitzer winner crackles with fresh energy, while Tom Stoppard's deeply personal **Leopoldstadt** offers a haunting meditation on Jewish identity and loss.

The season's diversity extends beyond awards pedigree, encompassing Jordan E. Cooper's provocative satire **Ain't No Mo'** and Mike Birbiglia's intimate solo show **The Old Man & The Pool**, which tackles mortality with characteristic wit.

Whether you're discovering these productions for the first time or revisiting favorites that have continued their runs, this guide offers insight into a season that balanced entertainment with substance, laughter with profound emotional truth.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays from 2023

As of March 2026, the Broadway plays that premiered in 2023 continue to demonstrate the remarkable vitality and range of American theater. This collection of ten productions—averaging an impressive 82/100 from critics—showcases everything from long-overdue revivals to bold new works that have redefined what's possible on stage.

Leading the field is Maria Friedman's acclaimed revival of **Merrily We Roll Along**, which has triumphantly rehabilitated Stephen Sondheim's infamous 1981 flop into an emotionally resonant success that critics now celebrate as definitive. Close behind, **Stranger Things: The First Shadow** proves that stage adaptations of popular IP can transcend mere fan service, with critics praising its technically stunning production values and theatrical ambition. Meanwhile, **Appropriate** has emerged as essential viewing, with Sarah Paulson leading a blistering ensemble through what many consider a modern masterpiece of family drama.

The year also brought significant revivals that speak to contemporary concerns: **Purlie Victorious** demonstrates the enduring relevance of Ossie Davis's 1961 satire, while **Parade** resonates with urgent timeliness. New voices found purchase as well, from Alex Edelman's solo tour-de-force **Just for Us** to the Pulitzer Prize-winning **Fat Ham**, which reimagines Hamlet at a Black family barbecue. Traditional Broadway fare like **Sweeney Todd** shares space with innovative work such as **Stereophonic**, an immersive three-hour rock drama that critics have hailed as near-perfect theater.

Whether you're seeking musical theater classics, provocative new plays, or technically ambitious spectacles, these ten productions represent the best of what 2023 brought to Broadway stages.

best-broadway-plays-2024.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in 2024

As we look back from March 2026, the 2024 Broadway season stands out as a remarkably diverse year that brought fresh voices and bold revivals to the stage. The ten productions featured here maintain an impressive average critic score of 85/100, reflecting a season where artistic ambition consistently met critical approval.

Leading the pack is **Stereophonic**, David Adjmi's meticulously crafted drama about a 1970s rock band in the studio. Critics have hailed it as a theatrical marvel, praising its authentic depiction of the creative process and its ability to capture the messy reality of artistic collaboration. The production's attention to period detail and emotional honesty has resonated deeply with reviewers.

**Maybe Happy Ending** represents another highlight—a robot love story that critics celebrate as one of Broadway's most original musicals in years. Its ability to find genuine emotion in an unconventional premise demonstrates the season's willingness to embrace unexpected narratives.

Comedy found its moment with **Oh, Mary!**, Cole Escola's irreverent reimagining of Mary Todd Lincoln as a cabaret-obsessed narcissist. The farce has earned near-universal acclaim for its riotous humor and audacious premise, proving that absurdist comedy still has a vital place on Broadway.

The season also delivered strong revivals, including George C. Wolfe's **Gypsy** featuring Audra McDonald's deeply moving interpretation of Mama Rose, and a lavish mounting of **Oliver!** that balances Dickensian darkness with Lionel Bart's beloved score.

Whether you're drawn to intimate dramas like **Mary Jane**, innovative dance-musicals like **Illinoise**, or spirited ensemble pieces like **Operation Mincemeat**, the 2024 season offers compelling options that continue to reward audiences well into 2026.

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:

As Broadway moves through the spring of 2026, the plays that opened throughout 2025 continue to demonstrate the medium's remarkable range and vitality. This month's top ten features an impressive average critic score of 84/100, reflecting a particularly strong season for dramatic work.

The season also includes timely revivals—**Ragtime** resonates with contemporary audiences thanks to Joshua Henry's powerhouse performance—and ambitious new work like **Liberation**, Lauren Yee's structurally complex feminist memory play that critics find both moving and thought-provoking.

For theatergoers planning their spring Broadway calendar, this collection offers compelling options across multiple genres and theatrical styles.
